PullRequest.Title: Fix configuration events when toggling tab focus mode
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes microsoft/monaco-editor#4740.

## Summary

Toggling tab focus mode with Ctrl+M changes keyboard navigation, but the computed `tabFocusMode` option ignores the global state. Configuration recomputation therefore detects no change and suppresses `onDidChangeConfiguration`.

Compute the option from the existing effective environmental value instead. This preserves global/per-editor precedence and lets the normal change-detection path emit the event, without changing shortcut handling or forcing notifications.

Add two regression tests covering initial state, multiple editors, global toggles, explicit per-editor options, and suppression of unchanged effective values.

## Validation

- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src\vs\editor\test\browser\config\editorConfiguration.test.ts --run src\vs\editor\test\browser\widget\codeEditorWidget.test.ts --reporter dot` — **50 passing**. Both new regression tests fail without the fix.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\editor\common\config\editorOptions.ts src\vs\editor\test\browser\config\editorConfiguration.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `npm run monaco-compile-check` — **passed**.
- `node .build\monaco-4740-browser\harness.mjs test` — **passed** using a local-only harness, not included in this PR. Browser-driven Ctrl+M, Tab, and Shift+Tab reproduce the baseline bug and verify the fix with two standalone editors, using both EditContext and textarea input.

Full Electron/application validation remains blocked by local environment issues: a missing Windows SDK and unrelated dependency resolution through a parent Yarn PnP manifest.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle global tab-focus mode through Ctrl+M or the editor.tabFocusMode configuration while multiple code editors are alive
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ToggleTabFocusModeAction/TabFocusMode calls TabFocus.setTabFocusMode, whose emitter synchronously invokes every live EditorConfiguration. Each configuration recomputes and compares all editor options; after this diff, editors whose effective tabFocusMode changes also synchronously notify the view model, view parts, context keys, and editor contributions before the action can finish. The all-options recomputation was already on this critical path before the PR; only the effective change notification is newly enabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cached browser font-metrics lookup, with synchronous DOM measurement only on an uncached font/window
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup per live editor on each TabFocus event; warm hits are O(1), while cold measurement is shared by the cache for editors with the same font/window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every TabFocus event already called _recomputeOptions for every live EditorConfiguration and therefore performed the same font-info lookup before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The lookup is synchronous on the toggle path, but an already constructed editor normally populated the cache. The PR does not alter this lookup or its cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live editor configurations whose effective mode follows the global value, including visible embedded editors. Explicitly enabled editors are filtered by equality. Duplicate sets to the same effective value recompute as before but emit no configuration event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: TabFocus's emitter delivers listeners synchronously and serially; there is no concurrency burst, queue, or asynchronous boundary. Work scales linearly with live editors and their synchronous configuration listeners.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: EditorConfiguration still performs the pre-existing font-info lookup during recomputation. FontMeasurements caches by window and BareFontInfo, so normal toggles are warm-cache reads; a cache miss can perform one DOM font measurement per distinct uncached font/window and is not introduced or made more frequent by the diff. Configuration equality suppresses duplicate effective values.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous linear notification fan-out and its before/after distinction, based on the TabFocus listener, EditorConfiguration equality path, CodeEditorWidget forwarding, view-model guards, and the added compute override. High confidence that external I/O/IPC/network/subprocess boundaries are absent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Monaco embedders can retain more live editors than the typical VS Code workbench, but the toggle is an explicit, infrequent user/configuration action and the newly reached handlers are predominantly option checks/no-op guards. No concrete expensive boundary or collection-wide reconstruction is newly reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The new fan-out is the required configuration notification, occurs only when the effective value changes, and is bounded by live editors on an infrequent action. The expensive all-option recomputation and possible font lookup already occurred before the diff; downstream wrapping reconstruction is equality-guarded and no new external boundary is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct an editor or update its per-editor tabFocusMode option while the global mode is either enabled or disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction validates and computes the registry once; updateOptions validates changed raw options, recomputes, compares, and synchronously emits only an effective change. The new EditorTabFocusMode.compute performs one environment-property read in place of the base option's value return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing browser font-metrics lookup during full editor-option computation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup for the editor per construction or effective raw-option update; cache misses are per unique font/window, not per option.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Construction and updateOptions already computed every registered option and read font metrics through the same cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous and pre-existing; the subclass replacement does not change whether or when this lookup occurs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time compute per editor construction or option recomputation. Updates affect one editor; cost does not scale with document length, history, or model size. If global mode is enabled, raw false/true updates that do not alter the effective result are now suppressed by equality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per calling editor with no added parallelism, limiter, queue, or fan-out to other editors.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same EditorConfiguration font cache behavior applies: construction may cold-measure a unique font/window, while subsequent updates are warm. The changed option compute adds no cache, invalidation, or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the registry loop, updateOptions call path, and tests covering effective-value suppression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the changed compute method is constant-time. The number of unrelated configuration consumers depends on the embedder, but equality suppresses events when the effective value is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. Initial computation has equivalent constant cost, and effective-value equality can reduce notifications for per-editor changes masked by the global mode.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced global toggles, editor construction, option updates, view-model propagation, embedded-editor forwarding, unfiltered contribution listeners, and the font-measurement cache. The PR introduces required, synchronous configuration-event fan-out when the effective global value changes, but not a concrete actionable performance regression: the heavy option recomputation and font lookup were already present, duplicate/effectively unchanged values are suppressed, downstream expensive reconstruction is guarded, and no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is added.
